description.narrative: The objective of the Road Safety Project for Argentina is to contribute to the reduction of road traffic injuries and fatalities in the Borrower's territory through the strengthening of the Borrower's institutional framework and management capacity for road safety and the reduction of road crashes in selected pilot corridors. There are three components to the project, the first component being institutional capacity building. This component will finance consultancy services, technical assistance (training), human resources, non- consultancy services and goods (hardware and software). The second component is the demonstration corridors and incentive fund program. This component will include two sub-components, (i) 'safe corridors' demonstration program (US$ 1.14 million), and (ii) incentive fund for the implementation of road safety policies and practices (US$ 10 million). The main aim of these two sub-components is to finance road safety initiatives that have a demonstrable effect on road safety improvements. Given that success begets success, this will then form a basis to catalyze, and encourage the national government and provincial governments to extend the tested approaches to other parts of the country's road network. Finally, the third component is the road safety monitoring and evaluation system within the national road safety observatory.

The proposed project development objective is to contribute to the reduction of road traffic injuries and fatalities in the Borrower's territory through the strengthening of the Borrower's institutional framework and management capacity for road safety and the reduction of road crashes in selected pilot corridors.

title.narrative: Number of provinces and municipalities that have developed strategic road safety plans.

comment.narrative: As part of the project, 262 strategic road safety plans were developed in provinces and municipalities. They were the Incentive Fund's first required intervention. The implementation of subsequent activities conformed to planning under a Safe System Approach. Strategic road safety plans were developed in 147 municipalities from 19 provinces.

title.narrative: Number of formal meetings per year of the Federal Council for Road Safety coordinated by ANSV during the Project.

comment.narrative: The ANSV led formal meetings of the FCRS four times per year as a means to achieve inter-sectoral and multi-jurisdictional coordination. Relevant ministries and provincial governments are represented in this council, which therefore became a key formal space, led by the ANSV, in which national road safety policy is discussed and actions are coordinated among sectors and jurisidictions. Leadin regular meetings of the FCRS enabled the ANSV to coordinate actions with different ministries and on the ground with provincial jurisdictions. Because of the broad autonomy that provinces have under Argentina's federal governance system and a lack of formal spaces to coordinate policy in the area of road safety prior to the agency's creation, the FCRS, supported by the Incentive Fund, was key in obtaining provinces adherence to Federal Road Safety policies, enriched by civil society monitoring of actions and targets and provision of feedback through the Consultative Committee, which is part of the ANSV's governance structure. This indicator was revied during the 2015 restructuring process. The change consisted of removing the reference to “project coordination” because the meeting's issues go beyond project coordination; replacing the word “managed” with “coordinated” to reflect the agency's current role; and changing the word “periodic” with “per year”. The target was also changed from “6 (six)” to “4 (four)” to reflect the changes in the FCRss internal legislation that defines the number of periodic meetings as every three months, between March and December of each year. Three meetings were held in the second half of 2010, five in 2011, and four in 2012, 2013 and 2014, respectively. Meetings were held in Puerto Iguazú, Ciudad de Salta, and Puerto Madryn in 2015. Meetings were held in Ciudad de La Rioja, Ciudad de Córdoba, Rosario, and San Salvador de Jujuy in 2016. At project completion, in the first half of 2017, two formal meetings were held in Ushuia (Tierra del Fuego) and Ciudad de San Juan, and two others took place in the second half of 2017 in Entre Rios and Tucuman.

title.narrative: Number of successfully delivered road safety education campaigns and workshops.

comment.narrative: This indicator considers road safety education workshops, awareness campaigns, road safety conferences and educational talks given by the agency to school teachers, students and the general public each year. This indicator measures the annual number of campaigns and workshops delivered, in order to monitor the continuity of these activities. In the first half of 2017, 588 of these activities were delivered, but the yearly amount could be even higher. In 2010, 167 activities were delivered; 592 in 2011; 1,471 in 2012; 279 in 2013; and 527 in 2014. In 2015, 394 workshops and 210 awareness campaigns were delivered, totaling 604 activities; and in 2016, 404 activitiess were delivered. An impressive total of 4,632 education campaigns and workshops were delivered during project execution.

title.narrative: Creation of a national driver license registry system.
Creation of a national traffic records and infractions registry system.

comment.narrative: The creation of a national driver's license registry system was supported by the creation of a national traffic records and infractions system, which could only be implemented in any given province if it opted in. The purpose is to verify the driving records of applicants to establish their eligibility for a new license or renewal. Of a total of 24 provinces, the system was active in 11 provinces in 2011; 14 in 2013; 17 in 2014; and 19 in 2017.

title.narrative: National Road Safety Observatory public website functioning with updated official yearly data on traffic crashes, fatalities and injuries, and related contributing factors (human, vehicle and road), a

comment.narrative: The National Road Safety Observatory's public website, which has been functioning since 2012, facilitates public access to road safety information. It has aggregated data from Argentina's 24 provinces and is updated to 2016.

title.narrative: Number of selected hospitals (trauma centers) with a road injury information system.

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the cumulative number of hospitals (trauma centers) with a road injury information system. The target was defined during project execution to ensure coordination and agreement with the Ministry of Health. 12 hospitals along demonstration corridors report injuries through the TRAUMA system to the Ministry of Health, in the Province of Buenos Aires. The other 38 hospitals report injuries through the SIVILE system to the National Ministry of Health, totaling 50 hospitals with a road injury information system and a 416% achievement of the target.

title.narrative: Usage of seat belts in the "Safe Corridors".

comment.narrative: This percentage value corresponds to the average use of seatbelts (by drivers, passengers and other occupants) in the "safe corridors," measured through observational studies with the following results: 64.10% in 2012, 59.33% in 2013, 67% in 2014, and 95.5% in 2017. These observational studies were not conducted in 2015 and 2016 because the ANSV received expert recommendations to perform them more spaced in time. The percentage of compliance at national level was 43.6% in 2016. (In the United States, as a reference, there was 89% compliance in 2016.)

title.narrative: Number of road Police partnership and inter-jurisdictional joint operations by traffic enforcement forces with ANSV.

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the annual number of road police partnerships and inter-jurisdictional joint operations by traffic enforcement units with the ANSV, because coordination of traffic enforcement units was an ongoing effort throughout project execution. There were 12,155 road police partnerships and inter-jurisdictional joint operations by traffic enforcement units with the ANSV during the first half of 2017, representing a 608% achievement of the target. The total number was 27,518 in 2016; 21,775 in 2015; 20,501 in 214; 29,850 in 2013; 31,513 in 2012; 28,997 in 2011; and 9,943 in 2010. A total of 184,252 inter-jurisdictional joint operations were conducted during project execution.

title.narrative: Reduction in the death rate (number per 1 million veh-km) on the selected corridor sections

comment.narrative: The death rate (number per 1 million veh-km) for 2010 was 0.018 in the selected corridors. The final target was a 20% reduction of this rate compared to 2010; the baseline was a 0% reduction. A semi-annual rate of 0.012 was achieved as of June 2017, representing a 22.92% decrease with respect to the same period in 2010. In 2011 and 2012, the average annual death rate was 0.018, representing a 0% decrease with respect to the 2010 death rate. In 2013, 2014, 2015, and 2016, the death rates were 0.017, 0.012, 0.016 and 0.013, respectively. These represented a 7.27% reduction in 2013 compared to the 2010 death rate, a 34.55% reduction in 2014, a 12.73% redction in 2015, and a 30.91% reduction in 2016.

title.narrative: Reduction in the number of reported non-fatal road traffic injuries on the selected corridor sections.

comment.narrative: The number of reported non-fatal road traffic injuries in the selected corridor sections in 2010 was 269 (annual value). The ultimate goal was to reduce this number (in absolute values) by 20%; the baseline was a 0% reduction. The unit of measurement used for this indicator is the percentage reduction of absolute values compared to 2010 values. As of June 2017, a 14.62% reduction was achieved in relation to the first half of 2010 (130 serious injuries). The number of serious injuries in 2011 was 247, representing a 8.18%eduction compared to 2010; in 2012 there were 274 serious injuries, representing a 1.86% increase compared to the baseline year. In 2013 and 2014, there were 246 and 226 serious injuries, respectively, representing a decrease of 8.55% and 15.99%, respectively, copared to 2010. In 2015 the reduction compared to the baseline year was 23.05% (207 serious injuries), and in 2016, 36.06% (172 serious injuries). Although the reduction reported in 2017 does not reach the target, this value was only for the first half of the year. The trend from the preceding years shows that the target was achieved.

title.narrative: Number of road safety training workshops delivered to traffic enforcement units

comment.narrative: This indicator considers training workshops delivered yearly to traffic enforcement units, encompassing municipal traffic agents, control agents, speed-radar operators, police, firemen and civil defense. The baseline is 19, which was the number of workshops delivered in 2010. The target was lower than the baseline because the objective was to achieve a continuous, sufficient level of training, which was exceeded. In the first half of 2017, 1,148 members of traffic enforcement units were trained in 37 workshops, representing a 616% achievement of the target. In 2016, 4,076 were trained in 95 workshops, representing a 1,583% achievement of the target. In 2015, 35 workshops were delivered with the participation of 729 people. In 2014, 35 workshops were delivered, at which 1,738 people were trained. There were 26 workshops in 2013, 33 in 2012, and 30 in 2011. A total of 310 workshops were delivered during project execution.

title.narrative: Compliance with speed limits in the "Safe Corridors".

comment.narrative: This percentage value corresponds to the level of compliance with speed limits for light and heavy vehicles. Compliance was at 88.60% in 2011, 93.10% in 2012, 94.60% in 2014, and 99.30% in 2017.
